title: Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning for Nonstationary Robot Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2611.19251v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reasoning about what an action will cause requires internalizing how a system behaves. As conditions seldom stay fixed, this must often happen within a few interactions. Yet systems that look identical in a snapshot can respond differently to the same action, depending on physical conditions the snapshot hides. Context-based models capture this separation by summarizing recent transitions into a latent context, but do not specify how that context should change the equations of motion. Physics-informed neural networks build those equations into the model, but describe only a single system and cannot recognize when it has changed. We present Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning (PICR), which bridges the two. translated_title: 面向非平稳机器人动力学的物理信息因果推理
translated_abstract: 推理一个动作会产生什么后果，需要内化系统的行为方式。由于环境条件很少保持固定，这种内化往往必须在少数几次交互中完成。然而，在快照中看起来相同的系统，可能会对同一个动作做出不同的响应，这取决于快照所隐藏的物理条件。基于上下文的模型通过将最近的转移总结为潜在上下文来捕捉这种分离，但并未说明该上下文应如何改变运动方程。物理信息神经网络将运动方程构建到模型之中，但只能描述单一系统，无法识别系统何时发生了变化。我们提出了物理信息因果推理（PICR），将两者结合起来。只有从最近交互中重新推断出的上下文会被更新；它对一个固定的物理信息网络进行条件化，该网络决定机器人的惯性和势能，从而使机器人能够根据自身经验适应新的物理条件。
tldr: 该论文提出物理信息因果推理（PICR）方法，通过仅更新从少量近期交互中重新推断的潜在上下文来条件化一个固定的物理信息网络（决定机器人的惯性与势能），从而弥合基于上下文的模型与物理信息神经网络之间的差距，使机器人能在少数交互内适应新的物理条件。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning (PICR), which bridges context-based models and physics-informed neural networks by updating only a latent context re-inferred from recent interactions to condition a fixed physics-informed network governing the robot's inertia and potential energy, enabling rapid adaptation to new physical conditions within a few interactions.
